definition: based on chance or personal choice rather than reason
examples: The border between the two countries was drawn in an arbitrary way.
The choice of starting point was arbitrary.

definition: to make a process work by machine without people
examples: Many factories have automated their production lines.
Automation has reduced the number of workers needed in many industries.

definition: an unfair preference for or against something
examples: Researchers must avoid bias when they select participants.
The survey results were biased toward city residents.

definition: a diagram that shows information clearly
examples: The chart shows population growth over fifty years.
Early sailors charted the coastlines of unknown lands.

definition: to make something easier to understand
examples: The professor clarified the main points of the lecture.
The new rules need further clarification.

definition: a product that can be bought and sold, such as grain or oil
examples: Coffee is one of the most widely traded commodities.
The price of a commodity depends on supply and demand.

definition: to add to something in a way that improves it
examples: The museum's new wing complements the original building.
Field work is a useful complement to laboratory research.

definition: to follow rules or accepted standards
examples: All new buildings must conform to safety regulations.
The results conformed to the predictions of the model.

definition: belonging to the present time; existing at the same time
examples: The gallery displays contemporary art.
Contemporary accounts of the battle describe heavy rain.

definition: to say or show that something is the opposite of what is true
examples: The new evidence contradicts the earlier theory.
There is a contradiction between the two reports.

definition: extremely important
examples: Bees play a crucial role in pollinating crops.
Clean water is crucial for public health.

definition: the system of money used in a country
examples: The euro is the currency of many European countries.
Some ancient societies used shells as currency.

definition: to be a sign or symbol of something; to mean
examples: In chemistry, the letter H denotes hydrogen.
A red flag on the beach denotes dangerous conditions.

definition: to notice or discover something that is hard to see
examples: Sharks can detect tiny amounts of blood in the water.
Early detection of the disease improves the chances of recovery.

definition: to move away from the usual or expected way
examples: The ship deviated from its course during the storm.
Any deviation from the standard procedure must be recorded.

definition: to force something or someone out of its usual place
examples: The flood displaced thousands of families.
An object fully submerged in water displaces a volume of water equal to its own volume.

definition: a play for the theater; an exciting or emotional event
examples: Ancient Greek drama included both tragedies and comedies.
The novel describes the drama of life during the war.

definition: happening at the end of a long process
examples: The trade dispute led to the eventual collapse of the alliance.
Most of the seeds eventually germinated.

definition: to show something publicly; to show a quality or sign
examples: The museum exhibits fossils from around the world.
The exhibition attracted thousands of visitors.

definition: to use something fully for profit; to treat someone unfairly for profit
examples: Early settlers exploited the region's rich forests.
Laws were passed to prevent the exploitation of child workers.

definition: to change frequently, especially up and down
examples: Prices fluctuate according to supply and demand.
Daily temperature fluctuations in the desert can be extreme.

definition: advice about how something should be done
examples: Doctors follow national guidelines when prescribing medicine.
The report includes guidelines for safe drinking water.

definition: to draw special attention to something
examples: The report highlighted the need for better roads.
One highlight of the conference was a talk on space exploration.

definition: suggested but not stated directly
examples: There was an implicit agreement between the two leaders.
The rules of the game were implicitly understood by all players.
